summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto focuses on Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She held a post as a research fellow (公募研究員) at Ryukoku University in 2012 and also studied there as a researcher (研究生, attested 2014).
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989 and later held a post there around 2003.

Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University by 2006 and served as a librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Tan Yun-shan, served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953, and was a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Yungfen Ma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (c. 1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), the EHESS, VTSIOM (~1988–2003), and the Levada Center (~2003–2006).
Yuri Mikhailovich Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.

Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University from around 1937 to 1941 and later served there as a professor from circa 1964 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, later holding professorships at Koyasan University and Nagoya University, as well as posts at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Esho Mikogami as a graduate student at Ryukoku University (attested 1982), lectured at Hanazono University (attested 1987), and served as assistant professor and professor at Ryukoku University.
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a position at Otani University and served at Doho University from circa 1972 to 2005, where he became Emeritus Professor.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996) and held positions at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, Gyoyu Tokiwai, and Hidenaka Tanaka, and later under Naoshiro Tsuji. He taught at Kyoto, Tokai, Tokyo Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka universities.
Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seio Okuda and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, studying under Louis Renou, Atsuuji Ashikaga, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He held posts at Kyoto University and Collège de France.

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1968–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history/archaeology, Japanology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education, the University of Tokyo, and Hitotsubashi University, later holding posts at Hitotsubashi and Kyoto University.

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He held posts at Kyoritsu University of Pharmacy and Kanagawa University.

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and Leipzig University under August Conrady, and later held a post at Peking University from circa 1923 to 1926.
